title: Private VPC — Cluster Overview & Actionable Status Panels
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, actionable cluster overview for Private/VPC deployments that surfaces network health, capacity, upgrade status, and recommended operator actions in an at-a-glance panel layout. The UI should scale to lists of clusters and allow team members to triage issues quickly without leaving the console.
background: Private deployments currently rely on several disconnected views: cluster list, network topology, and an upgrade timeline. Operators need a single coherent surface that summarizes status, highlights risky clusters, and provides contextual actions (reboot nodes, start maintenance, open support ticket). Existing flows cause context switching and slow incident response.
goals: 1) Create a single-row cluster card layout with key status indicators and primary actions. 2) Surface network-level alerts (peering, route conflicts) and capacity warnings. 3) Allow quick drilldowns to topology canvas or upgrade timeline. 4) Maintain privacy/compliance constraints for on-prem clusters.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Collapsible Cluster Panel that contains: summary bar (name, region, last-checkin, SLA status), three status chips (Network, Runtime, Upgrade), a capacity bar, and an overflow menu with operators actions. Expandable area reveals recent incidents, last 24h latency heatmap, and links to topology and upgrade history. Panels can be pinned and filtered by label (e.g., production, regulated).
acceptance_criteria: Collapsible panel renders correctly at 3 breakpoints (desktop, tablet, mobile)
Network, Runtime, Upgrade chips reflect backend status mappings (green/yellow/red) without requiring additional API fields
Primary actions (Open Topology, Schedule Maintenance, Create Support Ticket) operate via console modals or deep links
Pinning and filtering persists across sessions for each user
Performance: panels load in under 300ms for 50 clusters (backend mock acceptable for review)
design_notes:
- Use existing console token colors for status chips to keep global consistency.
- Capacity bar is normalized to cluster reservation size rather than absolute GPU count.
- Accessibility: ensure contrast ratios for status chips and keyboard focus for actions.
- Privacy: avoid showing customer identifiers for multi-tenant views; use hashed cluster aliases when required.
review_feedback: PM (Riley Parker): strong preference for a compact list mode by default; expand-by-click for operators who need detail.
Eng (Ben Ortiz): backend will expose a single aggregated /clusters/summary endpoint — confirm payload fields required (see ENG-2918).
Security (Maya Iqbal): confirm that pinning metadata doesn't persist cross-tenant; flagged for follow-up.
prototype_notes: High-fidelity prototype covers expanded + compact states. Interaction spec includes hover tooltips for last-checkin, and a keyboard shortcut (K) to focus the cluster list. Prototype includes micro-interactions for chip state transitions.
implementation_notes: Frontend: React + Tailwind components; reuse StatusChip and CapacityBar atoms. Backend dependency: ENG-2918 to add cluster.summary fields (upgrade_state, network_alarms, capacity_ratio). Feature flag: console.cluster_overview_v2 rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: exposing too many actions could enable accidental operator changes. Mitigation: require confirmation modals and tie destructive ops to RBAC checks. Risk: data volume for heatmaps. Mitigation: sample to 1-min resolution for list view and provide full-resolution in expanded drilldown.
next_steps: Iterate on compact-by-default variant per PM feedback (2 days)
Sync with ENG-2918 to finalize API contract (1 meeting)
Security review for pinning persistence and aliasing (submit SR-2026-03)
Create implementation tickets for frontend atoms and feature flag rollout
